title: Postgres connection pool exhaustion during post-deploy traffic spike
cause: HikariCP default connection pool limit (10) was exceeded when payment checkout webhook traffic surged after release v2.4.1.
error_log: org.postgresql.util.PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections (active: 100/100)
fix_worked: Increased Postgres max_connections to 350 and adjusted payments HikariCP maximumPoolSize=60 via configmap rollout.
fixes_failed: Blindly restarted payments deployment pods with 'kubectl rollout restart deploy/payments'. This caused a violent connection stampede upon startup, locking Postgres entirely and extending the outage by 18 minutes.

title: Redis OOM eviction storm causing session validation dropouts
cause: Session tokens stored without TTL expiration caused Redis memory to hit the 8GB maxmemory ceiling, triggering allkeys-lru eviction of active cache shards.
error_log: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory' (used: 8192MB / 8192MB)
fix_worked: Switched eviction policy to volatile-lru, expanded Redis shard memory to 16GB, and enabled TTL=86400 on session keys.
fixes_failed: Attempted FLUSHDB to clear memory. This triggered an immediate massive cache stampede onto the Postgres primary database, driving CPU to 100%.

title: 504 Gateway Timeout cascade due to search service degradation
cause: Search service degraded due to cold index, causing gateway HTTP client connections to block until the 60-second gateway timeout.
error_log: upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream: search.prod.internal:8080
fix_worked: Enabled Envoy circuit breaker with max_pending_requests=50 and configured fallback empty response for search suggestions.
fixes_failed: Increased proxy_read_timeout from 60s to 120s. This consumed all 10,000 available NGINX worker connections and froze all API traffic across the entire site.

title: Dead-letter queue accumulation due to proto schema mismatch
cause: Order processor v3.2 published payload with missing enum field, causing queue consumer deserialization panic and DLQ diversion.
error_log: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.exc.InvalidFormatException: Cannot deserialize value of type PaymentMethodEnum
fix_worked: Deployed consumer patch v3.2.1 with unknown enum fallback handler, then drained and redrove DLQ messages at 50 msg/sec.
fixes_failed: Ran batch redrive script 'ops queue redrive --all' without patching consumer. All 84,000 poisoned messages crashed the consumer pods in an infinite crash-loop.

title: Autovacuum wraparound freeze lock on orders table
cause: Long-running reporting query held shared transaction lock for 7 hours, blocking autovacuum from truncating dead tuples.
error_log: WARNING: database 'production' must be vacuumed within 1845214 transactions before transaction ID wraparound
fix_worked: Terminated blocking query PID via pg_terminate_backend and initiated VACUUM ANALYZE (PARALLEL 4) orders.
fixes_failed: Restarted the Postgres primary instance. Postgres had to replay WAL logs and perform crash recovery for 45 minutes before accepting writes.

title: JWT verification latency spike following certificate rotation
cause: JWKS URI cache was set to 0 seconds in auth-service config, forcing an outbound HTTPS roundtrip to the identity provider on every single request.
error_log: JWKS fetch latency 480ms from idp.prod.internal; threadpool exhaustion in auth-worker
fix_worked: Updated auth-service config to cache JWKS public keys in-memory for 1 hour with a 10-minute stale grace period.
fixes_failed: Scaled auth replicas from 4 to 20. This amplified outbound HTTPS traffic to the IDP, triggering IDP rate limiting (HTTP 429) and completely disabling logins.

title: Order creation 500 error due to database sequence integer overflow
cause: orders_id_seq reached maximum integer value (2,147,483,647) because column type was INT4 instead of BIGINT.
error_log: ERROR: integer out of range in sequence 'orders_id_seq'
fix_worked: Migrated column to BIGINT using ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN id TYPE BIGINT with zero-downtime shadow column procedure.
fixes_failed: Attempted 'ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN id TYPE BIGINT' directly during peak hours. This acquired an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the 50GB table, locking writes for 20 minutes.

title: ML ranker inference p99 latency spike due to glibc malloc fragmentation
cause: Repeated creation and destruction of dynamic tensor arrays caused resident memory fragmentation in PyTorch C++ wrapper.
error_log: RSS memory at 94% (15.2GB/16GB) without active batch load; jemalloc arena contention
fix_worked: Preloaded jemalloc library (LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libjemalloc.so) and configured MALLOC_CONF='dirty_decay_ms:1000,muzzy_decay_ms:1000'.
fixes_failed: Increased pod memory limit from 16GB to 32GB without fixing allocator. The leak consumed 32GB within 4 hours, causing node-level OOM killer to terminate kubelet.

title: Elasticsearch cluster state RED due to unassigned replica shards
cause: Data node disk usage exceeded 85% flood-stage watermark after bulk product index reindexing.
error_log: cluster_block_exception: blocked by: [TOO_MANY_REQUESTS/12/disk usage exceeded flood-stage watermark]
fix_worked: Purged temporary snapshot indices, lowered retention, and dynamically increased cluster flood-stage watermark to 92% to re-enable write indices.
fixes_failed: Force-assigned replica shards using cluster reroute with 'allocate_empty_primary'. This caused permanent silent loss of 120,000 product search indices.

title: Double billing risk due to Stripe webhook idempotency race condition
cause: Distributed lock in Redis for charge.succeeded was using non-atomic GET then SET, allowing concurrent webhooks to process twice.
error_log: WARN: Duplicate transaction processing attempt detected for external_id: ch_3N8e12918
fix_worked: Replaced lock acquisition with atomic Redis SET key value NX EX 30 and enabled database unique constraint on payment_transactions(external_id).
fixes_failed: Disabled webhook ingress temporarily to avoid double charges. Customers were charged by Stripe but orders were never fulfilled, generating 400 support tickets.

title: Order status notification delay due to thread pool starvation
cause: Asynchronous email sender used synchronous HTTP client blocking the shared Tomcat common worker thread pool.
error_log: java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException: Task rejected from java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor@41a (pool size 200, active 200)
fix_worked: Isolated email and push notification dispatches to dedicated bounded thread pool with non-blocking WebClient.
fixes_failed: Increased maxThreads in server.xml from 200 to 1,000. Under heavy load, this exhausted OS thread handles and caused kernel memory thrashing.

title: TLS handshake failure rate elevated after ingress controller update
cause: New ingress controller version defaulted to strict TLSv1.3 with deprecated cipher suites, disconnecting older mobile clients.
error_log: SSL_do_handshake() failed (SSL: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure)
fix_worked: Restored TLSv1.2 compatibility ciphers (ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256) in ingress-nginx ConfigMap.
fixes_failed: Generated and installed a new wildcard TLS certificate. The cipher mismatch was protocol-level, so the new certificate did not resolve handshake failures.

title: Postgres replica lag exceeded 60 seconds causing stale catalog reads
cause: Replica was running heavy analytics queries that conflicted with incoming WAL replication stream, triggering recovery conflict pauses.
error_log: FATAL: terminating connection due to conflict with recovery (User query might have needed to see row versions that must be removed)
fix_worked: Set max_standby_streaming_delay=30s on replicas and routed analytical queries to dedicated read-only warehouse replica.
fixes_failed: Increased hot_standby_feedback=on without safety monitoring. This prevented the primary from vacuuming deleted rows, bloating table size by 40GB.

title: Redis eviction storm on auth tokens during morning peak
cause: Marketing campaign sent 500,000 push notifications at 9:00 AM; user token creations exhausted Redis maxmemory shard.
error_log: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory' in redis-auth-shard-01
fix_worked: Provisioned additional 4GB shard for auth redis cluster and configured token TTL to 4 hours with sliding refresh.
fixes_failed: Restarted Redis container. Without persistent append-only files loaded, every user session was instantly invalidated, forcing 150,000 concurrent relogins.

title: RabbitMQ high memory alarm blocking producer publishers
cause: Unacknowledged messages on orders-fulfill queue accumulated past 100,000 because consumer concurrency was capped at 2.
error_log: connection refused: [vm_memory_high_watermark] memory limit (0.4) reached, blocking publishers
fix_worked: Scaled consumer deployment to 12 replicas and configured prefetch_count=20 to quickly drain backlogged queue.
fixes_failed: Purged the queue via management console. 14,000 active customer orders were permanently erased from the fulfillment pipeline.

title: Search index latency spike caused by unoptimized wildcard queries
cause: Frontend search box permitted leading wildcard queries (e.g. '*phone*'), bypassing inverted index and forcing full table scans.
error_log: Search query took 4200ms; Lucene regex query execution exceeded max_clause_count
fix_worked: Added frontend query sanitizer to strip leading wildcards and deployed ngram tokenizer for partial string matching.
fixes_failed: Increased Elasticsearch query thread pool size to 64. CPU immediately spiked to 100% across all 3 search nodes.

title: Payments connection pool starvation after Friday microservice deploy
cause: Payments service release v2.9.0 introduced unclosed Hibernate EntityManager sessions inside payment retry loops.
error_log: HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30005ms (active=50, idle=0, waiting=120)
fix_worked: Rolled back payments service to v2.8.9 and verified DB connection pool returned to 8 idle connections.
fixes_failed: Attempted 'kubectl scale deploy/payments --replicas=10' to handle load. Adding 5 more replicas multiplied the leaked connections and completely exhausted Postgres connections.

title: CUDA out of memory error during feature vector calculation
cause: New recommendation model weights were 2x larger than previous checkpoint, leaving insufficient VRAM for batch size 128.
error_log: torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB (GPU 0; 15.78 GiB total capacity; 15.30 GiB already allocated)
fix_worked: Reduced batch size to 64 and enabled mixed precision FP16 inference in model serving configuration.
fixes_failed: Restarted Triton inference server without changing batch size. It immediately crashed on the first inference batch with the same CUDA OOM.

title: DDOS volumetric flood on /api/v1/search endpoint
cause: Distributed bot scraper targeted unauthenticated search endpoint from 1,200 residential IP proxies.
error_log: NGINX limit_req zone 'search_per_ip' exceeded: 429 Too Many Requests, rate 12,000 rps
fix_worked: Activated Cloudflare Under Attack mode and deployed rate-limiting rule on /api/v1/search capped at 15 req/min per IP.
fixes_failed: Attempted manual iptables IP block on host. The botnet rotated IPs faster than iptables could be updated and iptables rules slowed kernel routing.

title: Postgres connection pool exhaustion on payments service (Recurring Friday Pattern)
cause: Recurring issue: Payments microservice database connection pool exhausted following deploy during high checkout volume.
error_log: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections (active: 300/300) from payments-worker
fix_worked: Deployed PgBouncer transaction-mode connection pooler in front of Postgres and tuned payments HikariCP pool to max 20 connections per pod.
fixes_failed: CRITICAL FAILED FIX: Restarting payments pods ('kubectl rollout restart deploy/payments') caused a violent reconnection storm that brought Postgres down.
CRITICAL FAILED FIX: Scaling up payments replicas multiplied active DB connections and caused database kernel panic.

title: Kafka consumer group rebalance storm during deployment
cause: Long message processing time exceeded max.poll.interval.ms (300000ms), causing Kafka coordinator to treat consumer as dead and trigger rebalance.
error_log: org.apache.kafka.clients.consumer.CommitFailedException: Commit cannot be completed since the group has already rebalanced
fix_worked: Increased max.poll.interval.ms to 600000ms and reduced max.poll.records from 500 to 50 in consumer properties.
fixes_failed: Restarted all Kafka broker nodes. This threw every topic into leader election and halted message processing across all services for 12 minutes.

title: Disk I/O saturation on EBS volume due to unindexed foreign key lookup
cause: New release added payment_events table without index on order_id, causing nested loop sequential scans on 40M rows.
error_log: iostat showing 100% %util on /dev/nvme1n1; read IOPS throttled at 3000 baseline
fix_worked: Created index concurrently: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_payment_events_order_id ON payment_events(order_id);
fixes_failed: Ran 'CREATE INDEX idx_payment_events_order_id ON payment_events(order_id)' without CONCURRENTLY. This locked the table and blocked checkout transactions.

title: LDAP directory synchronization timeout locking corporate SSO
cause: Corporate Active Directory domain controller unreachable on port 636 due to expired firewall rule, blocking internal admin logins.
error_log: javax.naming.CommunicationException: simple bind failed: ad.corp.internal:636 [Root exception is java.net.SocketTimeoutException: connect timed out]
fix_worked: Failed over to secondary domain controller ad2.corp.internal and restored security group egress rule.
fixes_failed: Bypassed LDAP auth in configuration. This permitted unauthenticated access to admin endpoints and violated SOC2 compliance.

title: RabbitMQ file descriptor exhaustion on socket connections
cause: Microservices opened new AMQP connection for each message instead of reusing channels on persistent connections.
error_log: file_descriptors_used (65536/65536) limit reached. Erlang VM cannot allocate sockets.
fix_worked: Updated client library to use connection pooling with singleton AMQP connection and pooled channels.
fixes_failed: Increased ulimit -n to 1,000,000 on the host without patching client code. The leak consumed memory until the node ran out of RAM.

title: Stale search results due to Kafka indexer lag
cause: Product update events backlogged because indexer consumer batch size was 1 item per bulk request.
error_log: Consumer lag for topic 'product-catalog-updates' is 382,000 messages (growing at 500 msg/sec)
fix_worked: Batch-buffered consumer writes into 500-item bulk requests to Elasticsearch, clearing the lag in 4 minutes.
fixes_failed: Restarted search indexer pods. The consumer restarted from the last committed offset and processed single records even slower.

title: Redis failover replication break due to slow sync buffer overflow
cause: Heavy write traffic exceeded client-output-buffer-limit slave 256mb 64mb 60, causing replica to disconnect and loop in full resync.
error_log: SYNC with master failed: Client output buffer limit exceeded on replication link
fix_worked: Increased client-output-buffer-limit slave to 1024mb 256mb 300 and enabled diskless replication in redis.conf.
fixes_failed: Promoted the desynchronized replica to master. This wiped 3 hours of recent customer session data that had not replicated.

title: Deadlock in orders inventory reservation under concurrent flash sale
cause: Transactions acquired row locks on items in arbitrary order instead of sorting item IDs, creating circular lock dependency.
error_log: ERROR: deadlock detected; Process 14201 waits for ShareLock on transaction 891; Process 14205 waits for ShareLock on transaction 890
fix_worked: Updated order checkout service to sort item IDs in ascending order before acquiring SELECT FOR UPDATE locks.
fixes_failed: Set deadlock_timeout to 10ms. This caused 90% of checkout transactions to immediately abort without attempting to succeed.

title: Payments gateway connection pool starvation and database connection drop
cause: Postgres max_connections saturated due to leaked connections in payments settlement batch job.
error_log: FATAL: sorry, too many clients already (max_connections=350 reached) from payments pod
fix_worked: Terminated idle payments settlement connections with pg_terminate_backend and capped batch job pool size to 5.
fixes_failed: CRITICAL: Restarting payments pods triggered a reconnection wave that kept Postgres CPU at 100% for 30 minutes.

title: Kong Ingress memory leak caused by unbuffered lua logging plugin
cause: Custom Lua logging plugin appended raw request bodies to global table without clearing references, leaking memory in Lua VM.
error_log: luajit: not enough memory while running log phase in custom-audit-logger
fix_worked: Disabled custom-audit-logger plugin and migrated to native OpenTelemetry sidecar collector.
fixes_failed: Increased container memory limit to 8GB. LuaJIT has a 2GB 32-bit address space ceiling and crashed anyway.

title: CPU throttling on ML ranker pods due to CFS quota period mismatch
cause: Kubernetes CPU limit was set to 2.0 cores with default CFS quota period 100ms; multi-threaded numpy burst exceeded quota in first 20ms.
error_log: container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total increasing at 85% rate; latency spike to 450ms
fix_worked: Set OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 and adjusted cpu limits to match requests (guaranteed QoS class).
fixes_failed: Set cpu requests to 0.1 cores. This resulted in node eviction during high cluster utilization.

title: Transaction ID wraparound emergency shutdown threshold approaching
cause: Forgotten long-lived prepared transaction (from aborted two-phase commit) held back datfrozenxid for 14 days.
error_log: WARNING: oldest active transaction ID is 200,000,000 away from wraparound shutdown
fix_worked: Identified orphaned prepared transaction via pg_prepared_xacts and executed ROLLBACK PREPARED 'tx_settlement_01'.
fixes_failed: Ran VACUUM FULL. This failed immediately because the transaction ID could not advance past the blocking prepared transaction.

title: Bcrypt hashing CPU saturation causing login queuing
cause: Bcrypt work factor was increased from 10 to 14 in configuration, increasing CPU calculation time from 80ms to 1280ms per password hash.
error_log: Thread starvation: CPU at 99.8% in org.mindrot.jbcrypt.BCrypt.hashpw; login queue depth 1,200
fix_worked: Reverted work factor to 10 in AuthConfig and implemented rate limiting on /login endpoint.
fixes_failed: Scaled auth pod count from 4 to 16 without reverting work factor. Saturated all physical node CPUs in the cluster.

title: Kafka partition skew causing single consumer lag backlog
cause: Producer was partitioning messages by date string instead of user ID, routing 100% of today's traffic to Partition 0.
error_log: Partition 0 consumer lag: 250,000 messages. Partitions 1-15 consumer lag: 0 messages.
fix_worked: Patched producer partitioner key to use murmur2 hash of customer_id, redistributing load evenly across all 16 partitions.
fixes_failed: Added more consumer pods to the consumer group. In Kafka, only one consumer can read from Partition 0, so extra consumers sat completely idle.

title: Elasticsearch JVM GC pause stop-the-world incident
cause: Heap memory was allocated at 48GB, disabling Compressed Ordinary Object Pointers (Compressed OOPs) and ballooning memory overhead.
fix_worked: Configured ES_JAVA_OPTS to -Xms31g -Xmx31g to re-enable 32-bit compressed OOPs and switched to G1GC.
fixes_failed: Increased heap size to 64GB. Stop-the-world garbage collection pauses lengthened from 14 seconds to 38 seconds.

title: Outbound payment webhook TLS handshake timeout with payment gateway
cause: DNS resolution timeout for api.partner-bank.com due to local CoreDNS pod cache overflow.
error_log: java.net.UnknownHostException: api.partner-bank.com: Try again (CoreDNS SERVFAIL after 5000ms)
fix_worked: Enabled NodeLocal DNSCache on worker nodes and added static fallback IP in payments pod hostAliases.
fixes_failed: Restarted payments pods. The new pods also failed CoreDNS lookup and failed liveness probe, entering CrashLoopBackOff.

title: Redis lock lease expiration before long checkout transaction finished
cause: Payment gateway processing took 6 seconds, but Redis distributed lock TTL was hardcoded to 5 seconds, causing two checkouts to run simultaneously.
error_log: IllegalMonitorStateException: attempt to unlock read/write lock with token that has already expired
fix_worked: Implemented Redisson lock watchdog automatic lease extension with 30s ceiling.
fixes_failed: Removed the distributed lock entirely to prevent lease exceptions. Caused duplicate order creation on flaky networks.

title: HTTP/2 connection leak under mobile client network dropouts
cause: Gateway did not enforce keepalive_requests or client_body_timeout for half-closed TCP sockets from mobile cell tower handoffs.
error_log: socket leak: 45,000 CLOSE_WAIT sockets held open in gateway-proxy
fix_worked: Configured keepalive_timeout 65s, keepalive_requests 1000, and enabled SO_KEEPALIVE with 30s probe interval.
fixes_failed: Restarted the edge gateway pods. Caused an instant reconnect spike from 200,000 active mobile app users that overwhelmed auth.

title: Postgres shared buffers page eviction storm on heavy analytical query
cause: Ad-hoc query performed full table scan on 200GB orders_audit table, blowing out the 16GB shared_buffers cache.
error_log: Buffer pool hit ratio plummeted from 99.4% to 42.1%; disk read throughput peaked at 450MB/s
fix_worked: Cancelled query via pg_cancel_backend and added pg_prewarm to restore critical hot tables to memory.
fixes_failed: Increased shared_buffers to 48GB on a 64GB node without adjusting kernel shmmax. Postgres failed to start due to lack of OS shared memory.

title: Redis latency spike caused by KEYS * pattern scan in cron healthcheck
cause: Monitoring probe executed 'KEYS session:*' every 30 seconds on single-threaded Redis holding 8 million keys.
error_log: redis-cli slowlog: KEYS session:* took 2840ms, blocking all single-threaded command processing
fix_worked: Replaced KEYS command with cursor-based SCAN count 500 and cached key count metric in Redis info.
fixes_failed: Scaled Redis vertically. Because Redis is single-threaded for core command execution, higher core count had zero effect on KEYS command blocking.

title: Cold-start model artifact download delay on new pod scheduling
cause: Model weight download from S3 was 4.2GB, taking 90 seconds and triggering Kubernetes startupProbe failure.
error_log: Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503 (model weights downloading)
fix_worked: Mounted model artifacts from shared ReadWriteMany NVMe volume and pre-warmed weights on node init.
fixes_failed: Increased startupProbe failureThreshold from 10 to 60. Pods took 15 minutes to register during autoscaling spikes.
